diagnostic_evidence.quote: Theoretical analysis confirmed the convergence of the RCTZFIF to to the original data-generating function.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract and conclusion claim that the analysis proves convergence of the RCTZFIF to the classical FIF and to ψ. The bound in thm:convergence contains the term ‖ε‖∞ CΦ/(1−|λ|∞). Here Φ = max|f_j| is a data magnitude, and C = q/ξ equals 1 wherever q attains ξ. For any signature with some ε_j = 1, this term is independent of h and does not tend to 0. So even taken at face value, the theorem gives only an O(1) bound on ‖φ_ε−φ‖ and ‖φ_ε−ψ‖, not convergence.

failure_location.quote: Rigorous error analysis is presented to establish the convergence of the proposed zipper fractal interpolants to the underlying classical fractal functions, and subsequently, to the data-generating function.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either weaken the claim to a boundedness statement, or re-estimate the zipper term. The re-estimate would use |f_{j+1}−f_j| ≤ ‖ψ'‖∞ h together with the C^1 constraint |λ_j| < |a_j|, which forces |λ|∞→0. This would give a bound that is O(h).
issues.overall_effect: The advertised convergence of zipper interpolants, both to the classical FIF and to the data-generating function, is unsupported for every nontrivial signature.
issues.title: Convergence is claimed, but the stated error bound has a term that does not vanish as h→0
issues.why_classification: Restoring the convergence claim needs a contained re-estimation of the zipper term rather than new architecture. Otherwise an advertised conclusion has to be weakened.

issues.failure_explanation: For ε_j=1 the zipper map is reversed: L_{j,ε}(t)=L_j(t_1+t_n−t). On I_j, φ_ε(x) is evaluated at s'=L_{j,ε}^{-1}(x), while φ(x) is evaluated at s=L_j^{-1}(x), and s'=t_1+t_n−s. So φ_ε−φ equals λ_j[φ_ε(s')−φ(s)]+M_{j,ε}(s')−M_j(s), not λ_j(φ_ε−φ)+(M_{j,ε}−M_j) at a common point. The term φ(s')−φ(s) is not controlled by ‖φ_ε−φ‖, so the self-referential inequality and the resulting bound ‖M_{j,ε}−M_j‖/(1−|λ|∞) do not follow. Comparing M_{j,ε}(t) with M_j(t) at the same t produces nonzero f_{j+1}−f_j terms, even though both interpolants match at the knots. The derivative terms also use one a_j for both functions, although a_{j,ε}=−a_j when ε_j=1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must bound φ_ε against a correctly matched comparison function using its own functional equation. One option is the λ=0 zipper spline built with the reversed parametrization. The repair must also supply a classical error estimate for the reversed rational trigonometric pieces.
issues.overall_effect: The bound on ‖φ_ε−φ‖, the first term of thm:convergence, has no valid derivation, so the theorem's inequality is unsupported.
issues.title: Comparison of φ_ε with φ uses the same maps L_j, ignoring the reversed zipper maps for ε_j=1
issues.why_classification: The central comparison argument of the main error theorem collapses for every zipper signature. Replacing it needs a different decomposition that the source does not provide.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $h_j = la_j$, and by Theorem \ref{thm:rctfif}, we get

issues.failure_explanation: ξ is defined as the maximum of |q|, but the estimate replaces 1/q by 1/ξ in an upper bound. Since q ≤ ξ, we have 1/q ≥ 1/ξ, so the inequality goes the wrong way. The theorem then sets C = q_{j,ε}(θ)/ξ, which varies with θ and j, so the stated sup-norm bound is not expressed with a constant. The appeal to thm:rctfif, which bounds ‖ψ−φ‖, does not justify the bound on ‖M_{j,ε}−M_j‖.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep 1/q in each ratio. Then (αB_0+βB_1+γB_2+δB_3)/q = 1, or alternatively use min q > 0. Restate the theorem with a genuine constant, e.g. 2 in place of CΦ's coefficient.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed estimate of ‖M_{j,ε}−M_j‖ and the constant in thm:convergence are invalid or ill-defined.
issues.title: ξ = max|q| is used as a lower bound on q, and the constant C depends on θ
issues.why_classification: The theorem's constant must be redefined and the estimate redone. This is contained, but the statement as written is not established.

issues.failure_explanation: By the triangle inequality, the term −(2lδa_jB_2/πq)[d_{j+1−ε_j}−d_{j+1}] contributes +(2lδ|a_j|B_2/πq)|·| to an upper bound. The paper keeps the minus sign and obtains the factor [αB_1−δB_2], which can be negative and underestimates the error. The |f_{j+1}−f_j| term is also bounded by Φ rather than 2Φ.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use αB_1+δB_2 and the hypotheses β≥α, γ≥δ to get (αB_1+δB_2)/q ≤ 1. This recovers the (4h/π)η term. Also insert the factor 2 on Φ.
issues.overall_effect: The derivative part and the data part of the bound on ‖M_{j,ε}−M_j‖ are underestimated.
issues.title: Sign error in the triangle inequality: a negative term appears in an upper bound
issues.why_classification: This is a local correction using hypotheses already present, and the form of the bound survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $|\lambda_j| < a_j, j\in \mathbb{N}_{n-1}$ is the vertical scaling factor
By Theorem \ref{existence_of_rationalFIF}, the fixed point of the IFS

issues.failure_explanation: The endpoint conditions force a_j=(t_{j+1−ε_j}−t_{j+ε_j})/(t_n−t_1), which is negative when ε_j=1. Then |λ_j|<a_j and 0≤λ_j<min{a_i,…} admit no λ_j. So thm:positivity is vacuous for every signature containing a 1, including the experiments' ε=(1,…,1); there the bounds were in fact computed with |a_j| (0.1333=2/15). The C^1 property is justified by Theorem existence_of_rationalFIF. That theorem assumes non-reversed maps with a_i=(x_{i+1}−x_i)/(x_n−x_1)>0 and |α_i|<a_i^p, so it does not cover the zipper case.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace a_j by |a_j| in all scaling constraints. Then prove or cite a zipper C^1 version of the existence theorem: the derivative IFS F^{(1)}=(λd+M')/a_j is contractive iff |λ_j|<|a_j|, and endpoint derivative consistency must be checked for reversed maps.
issues.overall_effect: The positivity theorem never applies to genuine zipper signatures, and the C^1 smoothness of the RCTZFIF is unproved.
issues.title: For ε_j=1, a_j<0, so |λ_j|<a_j and condition 1 of the positivity theorem are unsatisfiable; a non-zipper theorem is invoked
issues.why_classification: The stated conditions need correcting, and a zipper analogue of the invoked smoothness theorem must be supplied. This is a contained argument, not new architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Our objective is to construct an RCTZFIF $\phi_\epsilon$ such that $\phi_\epsilon(t) > 0$ for all $t \in [t_1, t_n]$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof derives φ_ε(L_j(t))>0 from λ_jφ_ε(t)+p/q>0 by assuming φ_ε≥0 on [t_1,t_n], which is essentially the conclusion. The missing step is an invariance argument: the fixed-point operator maps the closed set of non-negative functions into itself when λ_j≥0 and M_{j,ε}≥0, so the fixed point is non-negative.

failure_location.quote: Assuming $\phi_\epsilon(t) \geq 0$ for all $t \in [t_1, t_n]$ and $0 \leq \lambda_j < 1$, it suffices to ensure

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standard argument that the contraction maps the closed cone of non-negative functions into itself, so the fixed point is ≥0. Strict positivity then follows from M_{j,ε}>0.
issues.overall_effect: The positivity conclusion is not validly derived as written.
issues.title: The positivity proof assumes φ_ε ≥ 0, which is circular
issues.why_classification: A short standard argument closes the gap, and the theorem is unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The text claims that the table's values satisfy thm:convergence, which requires γ_{j,ε} ≥ δ_{j,ε}. With δ_{j,ε}=1 for all j, every γ_j in the Fig. 1(a) row is below 1, and the other rows also contain γ_j<1. So the hypothesis fails.

failure_location.quote: Nevertheless, values as mentioned in Table \ref{table:rctzfif_params} satisfy Theorem \ref{thm:convergence}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the claim, or choose γ_j ≥ δ_j (e.g. γ_j ≥ 1).
issues.overall_effect: The numerical examples do not fall under the convergence theorem as claimed.
